subject: End-Q2 OKR scoring: disputed items + short narratives requested
messages:
From: Aditya Rao <aditya.rao@redwood.ai>
To: laura.bennett@redwood.ai, vivek.kulkarni@redwood.ai
Cc: marissa.cole@redwood.ai, ops-review@consulting.io
Date: 2026-07-01T08:12:00-07:00
Subject: End-Q2 OKR scoring: disputed items + short narratives requested

Team —

I ran the consolidated Q2 scoring pass and attached v2 of the CSV. There are three objectives where the raw metrics and the stakeholder testimony diverge enough that I think we need a short narrative to justify the final score for the QBR packet:

- O1 (Model latency platform-wide): score 65 -> product team argues 75 based on canary graphs; infra telemetry shows median improvements but p95 drift on high-concurrency windows.
- O3 (Cost/unit reduction via batching): score 40 -> ops claims 60 once planned cache changes land next sprint (not shipped this quarter).
- O5 (Enterprise adoption milestone - 3 pilot customers): score 66 -> commercial team counted a verbal commitment from Acme; procurement not complete.

Ask: can each owner (cc'd) provide a 2–4 sentence narrative for any objective they own that is contested, plus 1–2 lines of evidence (dashboard link, ticket id, or customer quote) by EOD Monday 07/05 so we can lock scores and produce a 1-page summary for execs.

Attached: q2_okr_scores_v2.csv (tracked changes), narrative template.

Quick notes on process: I biased toward conservative scoring where outcomes were not fully realized. If leadership wants an alternative bounding (optimistic vs conservative), say so and we can publish both in the appendix.

Thanks —
Aditya Rao
Head of Strategy Operations
Redwood Inference

Attachments: q2_okr_scores_v2.csv (text/csv), okr_narrative_vignette_template.docx (application/vnd.openxmlformats-officedocument.wordprocessingml.document)

From: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.ai>
To: aditya.rao@redwood.ai, vivek.kulkarni@redwood.ai
Cc: marissa.cole@redwood.ai
Date: 2026-07-02T10:05:00-07:00
Subject: Re: End-Q2 OKR scoring: disputed items + short narratives requested

Thanks Aditya — good pass. Inline responses below (keeps it tight for the packet):

> O1 (Model latency)
- I propose keeping final score at 70 (compromise). Rationale: majority of customer-facing surfaces saw median latency improvement of ~12% after kernel tuning (see Drive>Latency/June); however p95 regressions were linked to a single misconfigured pool (INC-4123) which ops fixed on 6/25. Evidence: Drive graph + INC-4123 log excerpt.

> O3 (Cost/unit batching)
- Leave at 40 in the main table. The proposed cache/batching bundle hasn't shipped; we should not credit future changes. Put 60 in appendix as "work-in-progress uplift" with clear note. Evidence: PR-884 (staged) + internal bench results.

> O5 (Enterprise adoption)
- Do not count Acme as closed. Move to 66 -> 50. Sales has an MOU but no signed SOW or PO. Evidence: Acme emails (sarah.jenkins@acme.com) + Procurement sync notes.

I'll attach a 3-sentence cover paragraph for the exec packet (below) and a one-line owner justification for each disputed objective in the CSV.

Exec cover paragraph (draft):
"Q2 delivered steady platform performance gains and important infra investments that position us to scale inference cost-effectively. While several technical levers demonstrated promising results, we held conservative scoring where outcomes relied on in-flight work or unsigned commercial commitments. The appendix documents optimistic uplift scenarios and recommended next steps to close the identified gaps."

Laura Bennett
VP, Product
Redwood Inference

---
Attachment: laura_q2_cover_paragraph.txt (inline)

From: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek.kulkarni@redwood.ai>
To: laura.bennett@redwood.ai, aditya.rao@redwood.ai
Cc: marissa.cole@redwood.ai
Date: 2026-07-03T15:10:00-07:00
Subject: Re: End-Q2 OKR scoring: disputed items + short narratives requested

Appreciate the quick triage. A couple of high-level directives so we align for the QBR:

1) We will keep the main scoreboard conservative (Aditya's baseline), and publish an "optimistic appendix" with uplift scenarios (Laura's wording looks good). The QBR slide must call out the assumptions for every optimistic uplift.

2) Final narratives: owners should send 1–3 bullets (max) describing the evidence and the single most important next action to close the gap. This will slot under each objective in the packet.

3) Responsibility / deadline: owners (Laura for product, Marissa for commercial, Aditya for ops decisions) — send final narratives + any final edits to q2_okr_scores_v2.csv to me and Aditya by COB Monday 07/05. I'll review and lock before we hand to comms. No extensions except escalated with reason.

4) For O5 (Acme): Marissa, loop in procurement thread and mark clearly "pilot" vs "contracted" in the packet. If Acme signs a PO before Monday close, we can reflect as contracted; otherwise we note pilot + next steps.

Vivek
Chief Revenue Officer (acting interim for QBR)
Redwood Inference
